circularity.note: These rows come from the same papers the rules were derived from. Agreement on them measures SELF-CONSISTENCY, not predictive accuracy, and must not be quoted as a validation result.

ground_truth_coverage.note: Most not-rescued rows record only that a null had a severe phenotype. Nobody measured whether a compensator went up, so they carry no ground truth on the axis the rule predicts. They can falsify an over-eager rule; they cannot confirm a correct one.

honest_accounting.verdict:
THE POSITIVE DIRECTION OF THIS RULE IS NOT RELIABLE, AND THE NUMBERS SAY SO.
  On the 13 case rows that are INDEPENDENT of the papers the rules were derived from, the rule chain agreed with the published outcome 4 times (31%) -- i.e. it was WRONG MORE OFTEN THAN RIGHT. All 9 of its independent errors are FALSE POSITIVES: it predicted a compensation response where the experimenters looked and found none.
  By contrast it scores 11/12 on the rows drawn from its own source papers. That gap between 11/12 on home ground and 4/13 away from it IS the result: the rule encodes the published mechanism faithfully and still does not predict new cases.
  CAUSE: the rule chain can only see a LESION CLASS, while the outcome turns on the individual ALLELE. El-Brolosy's own data contain two PTC alleles (hbegfa^sa18135, vcla^sa14599) of genes that do adapt, which do not adapt -- and the rule cannot tell them from the alleles that do. A PTC is necessary, not sufficient.
  WHAT THE NEGATIVE DIRECTION IS WORTH: 4 true negatives and 1 false negative. Refusals are far more trustworthy than assertions here, which is the asymmetry the scoring function should exploit.
  ON REAL DATA (mode A) the rule abstains on 24 of 40 rows and decides 1. Our omics layer cannot supply tissue-and-stage expression for a candidate compensator in almost every case, so in production this rule will mostly return 'unknown'. That is the correct behaviour and it should not be "fixed" by relaxing R06.
  RECOMMENDATION TO THE FUNCTIONAL SCORER: do NOT treat 'plausible-by-rule' as compensation. Count only 'documented' AND functional_rescue === true as a met requirement; treat 'plausible-by-rule' as an unmet requirement carrying a flag for human review. Use 'not-expected' with confidence.

distrust_classes.plausible-by-rule: do NOT count as met; flag for review
